rationale: deriv2 is a small C++ symbolic-differentiation benchmark (4.4 KB text, 19 functions) whose hot paths are recursive expression-tree walks with virtual dispatch (_ZN13quotient_expr5deriv at ~1.9 KB dominates), so control-flow obscuring passes get priority: FLA and IBR score highest since flattening plus bogus branches maximally obscure the recursion/switch structure an analyst would target, while SUB is weighted strongly as a near-free arithmetic diversifier that compounds well across the many small arithmetic-heavy deriv/print_m functions. BCF is kept high on security but tempered by elevated SizeCost/RuntimeCost weights because the binary is tiny and per-function BCF bloat would be proportionally conspicuous and slow the recursive traversals; SPLIT is enabled moderately to break up the two largest functions and feed IBR more regions. ICALL and IGV are deprioritized: the program's indirect calls are C++ vtable dispatch that ICALL-style indirection would slow (hot recursion, RuntimeCost 0.7) with risk of breaking vtable layout (CorrectnessRisk 0.3), and IGV's global-variable encoding offers little on this mostly stack/heap-object program while carrying the highest correctness risk of corrupting the C++ runtime's globals, so their low weights leave them applied only where features strongly justify it.
